newsitem.title: USA: ABC entertainment chief Harbert to resign.
newsitem.headline: ABC entertainment chief Harbert to resign.

text.p: In a surprise move, ABC Inc. said Tuesday Ted Harbert will resign next month as chairman of ABC Entertainment after nearly 20 years at the network.

Harbert, 40, had been responsible for all of ABC's Entertainment operations. But his duties were narrowed to supervising the division's finance and business affairs and overseeing late-night programming and the network's production ventures after ABC hired former NBC programming executive Jamie Tarses in June.

According to people familiar with his decision, Harbert met Monday with ABC Inc. President Robert Iger and told him he wanted to persue different opportunities. He then met with his staff Tuesday morning to inform them of his decision.
In a statement, ABC said Harbert's resignation is effective Feb. 15.
Harbert's decision comes at an awkward time for the network as it prepares to meet with more than 100 reporters this week for ABC's annual television critics conference.
According to terms of Harbert's contract with ABC, he had an opportunity to opt out by the end of January if the arrangement with Tarses was not working out.
Sources close to Harbert said while he respected Tarses and supported the decision to hire her, he wanted more responsibility.

"I have spent nearly 20 years at ABC and I am extremely proud of my contributions to this wonderful company," Harbert said in a statement. "However, it is time for me to seek out new challenges and opportunities in the second half of my career, which I look forward to eagerly."
Tarses, who was responsible for such NBC hits as "Friends", "NewsRadio" and "Mad About You", will assume responsibility for Harbert's duties.
ABC is currently the number two network behind NBC but it leads all networks in the key 18- to 49-year-old age bracket.
ABC is a unit of Walt Disney Co., which completed its $19 billion purchase of Capital Cities/ABC last year.
Disney's stock was unchanged at $69 on the New York Stock Exchange.
